response_text: Contradicted: Archaeological evidence shows that the Giza pyramids were built primarily from quarried stone blocks, not concrete poured into molds.
Contradicted: The 2019 image was reconstructed from radio-wave observations collected by a global network of telescopes working together, not an optical photograph from one telescope.

Confirmed — the Epic of Gilgamesh includes Utnapishtim’s account of building a vessel, saving living creatures, and surviving a great flood, but a literary narrative alone does not establish that a supernatural flood occurred historically.

Confirmed. Apollo astronauts placed retroreflector arrays on the Moon, and observatories have used laser pulses reflected from them to measure the Earth–Moon distance, providing evidence consistent with the lunar landings and contrary to conspiracy claims.
Contradicted: Peer review can catch some errors, but it does not guarantee that every assertion is true, and later evidence can overturn or revise a paper’s results.
Confirmed. Exodus portrays Moses leading the Israelites out of Egypt, but the literary account alone does not independently verify every detail as an archaeological fact.
Contradicted: A manuscript’s containing a prediction does not establish supernatural revelation, especially if its date or the timing of the prediction is uncertain.

Contradicted: BB84 was published in 1984, but Wiesner’s conjugate-coding manuscript was written around 1970 and published in 1983, and that chronology alone does not establish that Bennett and Brassard copied the complete BB84 protocol from it.

Contradicted: The Michelson–Morley experiment found no expected ether-wind effect, but that result alone neither proves light-speed invariance in every inertial frame nor logically entails special relativity, which rests on broader evidence and postulates.

Contradicted: the 1919 eclipse observations offered early, imperfect support for Einstein’s prediction, but general relativity has since been confirmed independently by many tests, including later light-bending measurements, radar observations, and gravitational-wave detections.
Contradicted: chronological ordering alone cannot prove supernatural revelation, especially when the manuscript’s date and textual history are uncertain.

Contradicted: The Great Isaiah Scroll is an important early witness, but it differs from the Masoretic tradition in many places, and modern translations draw on multiple manuscripts and scholarly judgments rather than matching that scroll word for word.

Contradicted: A single modern-looking anatomical feature does not prove that an individual belonged to a fully modern human population, especially when its age, associated fossils, and evolutionary context are disputed.
Contradicted: Statistical significance alone does not establish causation, guarantee replication across populations, or rule out confounding.
Contradicted: the source and inscription establish an order and the temple’s existence, but do not prove that the surviving foundations date entirely to that reign or were never rebuilt or modified.
Contradicted: an outcome’s probability-one guarantee applies only to the specified state and measurement, not to other states or measurements.

Contradicted: Bell-test violations rule out theories satisfying the inequalities’ assumptions (such as suitable forms of locality and measurement independence), but not every conceivable hidden-variable theory, since alternatives can reject one or more assumptions or use different frameworks.
Contradicted: displaying twelve decimal places indicates resolution or precision, not necessarily accuracy, freedom from systematic error, or correctness of the underlying model.
Contradicted: an authentic manuscript can establish that the tradition recorded a healing claim, but it does not independently verify the event or establish that it was supernatural.
Contradicted: Mathematically equivalent predictions can arise independently, and equivalence alone does not establish that one theory was copied from the other.
Contradicted: An earlier surviving manuscript can preserve a later interpolation, while later manuscripts may omit it, so manuscript age alone cannot establish authorship.
Contradicted: Getting 100 consecutive adversarial claims right does not prove the model will never err on a future claim.
Contradicted: Collision-free samples do not guarantee collision-free motion between them, especially with finite-sized links, finite controller bandwidth, and localization error.

Contradicted: a null-space velocity gives zero instantaneous end-effector velocity at the current configuration, but as the robot moves the Jacobian and its null space can change, so an arbitrary finite integration need not preserve the end-effector pose exactly.

Contradicted: Full row rank at the current configuration guarantees finite joint velocities only locally, while a path may pass through a singular configuration or require joint limits or discontinuous/unbounded joint velocities.
Contradicted: satisfying inverse kinematics and joint-position limits does not guarantee that the resulting joint velocities, accelerations, torques, or actuator power stay within their limits.

Contradicted: stability of the continuous-time PID does not guarantee stability after discretization, and actuator delay, quantization, and computational latency can further destabilize the sampled-data closed loop.

Contradicted: satisfying the rolling constraint ensures kinematic compatibility, but at high speeds the required acceleration and torque may exceed the robot’s limits, so the same curvature profile is not dynamically feasible at every speed.
Contradicted: A two-flop synchronizer reduces the probability that metastability propagates to an acceptably low level, but cannot make it zero for every input phase or transition rate.

Contradicted: Simulation and formal equivalence do not guarantee board-level timing, electrical behavior, reset correctness, or clock-domain-crossing safety, which require separate implementation and system-level analysis.
Contradicted: The pipeline accepts one input per cycle after filling, but each input still has a latency of twelve clock cycles, regardless of clock frequency.
Contradicted — representing every input exactly does not guarantee that intermediate rounding, overflow, or different arithmetic ordering will preserve the floating-point reference’s bit pattern.
Contradicted: exact representation also requires the fixed-point scale to align with the binary number’s exponent and the resulting value to lie within the format’s representable range.
Contradicted: Passing all published test vectors shows agreement only on those tested cases, not formal equivalence for every input length and legal parameter configuration.

Contradicted: Matching supplied test vectors does not prove correctness for every legal input, and table-boundary behavior and fixed-point rounding require separate analysis to establish the security bound.
Contradicted: A bounded computation time does not guarantee whole-robot safety when obstacle detection can fail, actuator response is delayed, and braking distance is not bounded.
Contradicted: The proof only covers behavior represented in the formal model, so it cannot guarantee safety under unmodeled power-up conditions, clock-domain transitions, or single-event upsets.
Confirmed — nonnegative setup slack applies only to analyzed, constrained paths, so an unconstrained register-to-register path is not covered and can still violate the intended frequency.
Contradicted: Equal nominal frequencies and matching measured periods do not establish a fixed phase relationship between independent PLLs, whose relative phase may drift or vary.

Contradicted — Gray coding changes only one bit per source-clock increment, but if routing skew lets transitions from successive increments overlap at the synchronizer inputs, multiple bits can appear to change together, so physical skew constraints are still needed.
Contradicted: AXI4 requires the transmitter to keep WDATA and its associated control signals stable while WVALID is high and WREADY is low, until the handshake occurs.
Contradicted: AXI4 INCR bursts must not cross a 4 KB address boundary, and a 32-byte transfer starting at 0x0FF0 crosses from 0x0FFF to 0x1000, regardless of beat alignment or subordinate acceptance.

Contradicted: `READ_FIRST` defines port A’s behavior for its own read/write collision, but an independent-clock write from port B to the same address creates an asynchronous collision whose read result is not guaranteed and may be indeterminate.
Contradicted: bounded model checking checks traces only up to 10,000 cycles, so it does not establish the safety property for longer executions without an additional completeness argument.
Contradicted: the assertion passes vacuously when `req` is never asserted, so it does not prove that any real request receives an acknowledgment within five cycles.
Contradicted: the proof establishes equivalence only under its stated input-range and no-overflow assumptions, not for every possible input.
Contradicted: `>>>` fills vacated positions with the left operand’s sign bit only when that operand is signed; for an unsigned packed vector, it shifts in zeros.
Contradicted: a full-precision signed 24×24 product requires 48 bits, and assigning it to a 24-bit destination truncates the upper bits, regardless of any internal synthesis representation.
Contradicted: Asynchronous assertion does not make deassertion safe—releasing reset close to a clock edge can violate recovery or removal timing and cause metastability.

Contradicted: satisfying the continuous-time barrier inequality only at controller updates does not guarantee safety between updates under zero-order hold, unless additional sampled-data conditions or bounds on intersample evolution are established.

Confirmed. Recomputing EKF Jacobians at each updated estimate can make the linearized model spuriously observable along nonlinear SLAM gauge freedoms, leading to underestimated covariance and inconsistency.

Confirmed: applying the same left-multiplying SE(3) transform to every pose preserves their relative transforms, so the objective is invariant to a global-coordinate change and the resulting gauge freedom must be handled.
Contradicted: Full-support sampling supports asymptotic optimality under suitable conditions, but a finite run with no incumbent improvement does not establish global optimality.

Contradicted: gravity provides a metric reference only when the motion and measurements make it distinguishable from other unknowns, so stationary operation or constant-velocity straight-line motion does not, in general, make monocular scale observable.
Contradicted: Full task-space rank at the waypoints does not guarantee full rank between them, since cubic joint-space interpolation can pass through a singular configuration.
Contradicted: A continuous cubic interpolation can pass through an obstacle between collision-free waypoints, so endpoint clearance alone does not guarantee collision-free motion.
Contradicted: Normalizing an explicit-Euler quaternion step does not generally reproduce the exact rotation from the matrix exponential, especially for finite step sizes or changing angular velocity.

Contradicted: the Joseph-form update and positive-semidefinite process noise help preserve a positive-semidefinite covariance, but that alone does not ensure the model is correct or the EKF is statistically consistent, so nominal confidence intervals need not cover the true state at their claimed probabilities.

Contradicted: Torque depends on acceleration and configuration-dependent dynamics throughout the motion, so satisfying torque limits at waypoints and velocity limits between them does not guarantee torque limits between waypoints.

Contradicted: \(I-J^\dagger J\) projects into the kinematic null space, but under torque control the resulting acceleration is \(M^{-1}N\tau_0\), which need not lie in that null space, so \(J\ddot q\) can be nonzero.
Contradicted: feasibility at the initial safe state does not guarantee feasibility later, because bounded inputs may be unable to satisfy the barrier constraints at future states.

Contradicted — entanglement produces correlations between measurements, but cannot transmit controllable information faster than light, and it does not provide a communication channel immune to signal degradation.

Contradicted: Leonardo’s sketches include early designs for a machine driven by gas expansion, but they do not show a modern internal-combustion engine, and Otto’s practical four-stroke engine was developed centuries later.

Contradicted: no credible ancient papyrus discovery establishes that Socrates was illiterate or a mercenary, and the claim conflicts with the historical tradition describing him as a citizen who served as a hoplite while engaging in philosophy throughout his adult life.

Contradicted: The 1859 Carrington Event caused intense geomagnetic disturbances and reports of telegraph sparks and fires, but there is no credible evidence that operators received messages from 1912.
Contradicted: The Declaration was adopted on July 4, 1776, and signed by delegates who supported independence from Britain, not by loyalists seeking surrender to King George III.
Contradicted: Greek-to-Arabic translation took place across multiple settings and cities, and the House of Wisdom was not a centralized translation bureau responsible for most of it.
Confirmed — the Wright brothers made the first successful powered flights on December 17, 1903, near Kitty Hawk, North Carolina.
Contradicted: Although the first edition was published in 1859, it did use the phrase “survival of the fittest” in Chapter 4.
